subject: Warning in run(timeoutMs)    #    no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf

messages.author: aebe473e7eb87f7e
messages.subject: Warning in run(timeoutMs)    #    no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
parts:
The following server.R code generates the warning when run locally on OS X:

Warning in run(timeoutMs) :
    #    no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf

When run on shinyapps.io it appears to kill the process after the first (successful?) rendering. Perhaps what generates this strange warning has a darker side-effect there.

The problem line is:
    rgg <- projectRaster(rgg, rgg.proj) # this line generates the warning

No warnings are generated when run as a code snippet.



library(shiny)
library(sp)
library(raster)
library(rgdal)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    depth <- as.numeric(input$depth)
    filepath <- 'data4jerry'
    filename <- paste(filepath,"/temp",sprintf("%03d", depth),"day00.dat",sep='')
    d <- read.table(filename,na.strings='-99.0000',dec='.')$V1
    d[which(d==-98)] <- NA    # it appears both -99 and -98 are missing values
    nx = 1501
    ny = 421
    
    d2 <- matrix(d,nrow=ny,ncol=nx,byrow=TRUE)
    d3 <- d2[nrow(d2):1,] # flip to match rendering order
    
#    EPSGproj = CRS("+init=epsg:3573")
#    EPSGproj = CRS("+init=epsg:5638")
    EPSGproj = CRS("+init=epsg:4326")
    EPSGproj = CRS(input$proj)
    lon = -30. + (1:nx-1)/60.
    lat = 62. + (1:ny-1)/60.
    rgg = raster(d3,xmn=min(lon),xmx=max(lon),ymn=min(lat),ymx=max(lat),
                 crs="+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84")
    
    # this projectRaster section generates a warning when run locally
    #  Warning in run(timeoutMs) :
    #    no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
    # and appears to kill the app on shinyapps.io after the 1st rendering.
    rgg.proj <- projectExtent(rgg, crs = EPSGproj)  # this line executes without warning 
    rgg <- projectRaster(rgg, rgg.proj) # this line generates the warning
    
    ice<-c('#2C537E','#346498','#3D74B1','#6797CB','#7AB2D2','#8DCDD8','#19FFCC','#65FF66','#B2FF33','#FFFF00','#FFC000','#FF8000','#FF4040','#D00000','#A00000')
    brks <- seq(-2,13)
    arg <- list(at=brks[seq(1,length(brks),2)], labels=brks[seq(1,length(brks),2)])
    plot(rgg,col=ice,breaks=brks,lab.breaks=brks,
        # xlim=c(min(lon),max(lon)),ylim=c(min(lat),max(lat)),
         cex.axis=1.25,cex.lab=1.25,axis.args=arg #,
        #main=paste(input$depth,"m,",strsplit(input$proj,"=")[[1]][2])
        )
    contour(rgg,add=TRUE,labcex=1.25)
    })

})

Any hints?
Thanks

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Warning in run(timeoutMs) # no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
parts: I doubt the warning would affect it. Does shinyapps::showLogs() (from the R or RStudio console) show anything interesting? If that doesn't give any clues, it's possible that your ShinyApps.io instance is running out of memory. If you log into the ShinyApps.io dashboard you should be able to increase the instance size for that app, which will increase the amount of available RAM.
